key_insight: OUCH combines pneumatic actuation with a focused indenter to evoke discomfort at approximately 89% lower applied force than a handheld pressure algometer in preliminary testing.
engineering_relevance: A compact wrist-worn device could standardize mechanical stimulation for neurological assessment while reducing reliance on variable manual application.
method: Stacked pneumatic pouch actuators drive a rigid indenter.
A compliant spacer buckles at a set load, allowing skin contact only during actuation.
Finite element analysis and physical testing characterize contact mechanics and tissue deformation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included blocked-force tests, clinician evaluation, finite element analysis, a deformable testbed, and preliminary perceptual testing; at 200 kPa inflation, estimated contact pressure reached 18,500 kPa—over 25 times the algometer tip's pressure.
watch_item: Preliminary discomfort results do not establish clinical assessment accuracy or repeated-use skin safety in patients with disorders of consciousness.
paper_title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
